scenes.name: The Yardbirds
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Salidos de la misma escena de blues del oeste de Londres que los Stones (heredaron su sitio en el Crawdaddy en 1963), dudaron entre el R&B purista y el pop; Eric Clapton se fue justo con su primer éxito y Jeff Beck abrió terreno nuevo. «Heart Full of Soul» fue de los primeros discos pop occidentales con modos indios (Beck imitó el sitar con la guitarra), «Still I’m Sad» partía de un canto gregoriano y su firma era el rave-up: blues acelerado hasta una serie de clímax, como las oleadas hormonales adolescentes. Keith Relf hablaba del pop como pintura abstracta, «imágenes en sonido». «Shapes of Things» (24 de febrero de 1966), grabado entre Chess y Columbia, es modernismo pop en su apogeo: ritmo marcial, letra filosófica y ecológica, drones de feedback y fizz casi de sitar. En la cara B, «You’re a Better Man Than I» de Mike Hugg atacaba el racismo y el militarismo.

scenes.name: Blues rock británico
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: La «gramática» del heavy: su estructura de canción, sus progresiones y sus riffs vienen del blues eléctrico urbano de Muddy Waters y Howlin’ Wolf, pero de segunda mano, ya «rockeado» por los grupos británicos de guitarra. El gran mediador son los Yardbirds y su sucesión de solistas (Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck y Jimmy Page), que veneraban a los bluesmen negros sin imitarlos servilmente. Cream (y Clapton, según él mismo) inventa el solo largo para estirar media hora de repertorio, y el público lo convierte en convención. El virtuosismo de la guitarra solista es la mayor herencia del blues rock al heavy.

scenes.name: Led Zeppelin
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: La otra banda fundadora, preferida por los estadounidenses: para Pete Fornatale fijaron los estándares que todos los que vinieron detrás deben cumplir. Jimmy Page la formó al salir de los Yardbirds con el nombre de New Yardbirds; según la leyenda, Keith Moon profetizó que caerían «como un zepelín de plomo». Page y Robert Plant son el gran ejemplo del doble foco guitarra-voz del heavy, una rivalidad afectuosa en la que ninguno eclipsa al otro, y los aullidos de Plant son uno de los modelos del canto del género. Sus temas más dulces fueron siempre carne del formato de radio hard rock.

podcast.title: Accused of Plagiarism for "Stairway to Heaven"
podcast.body: Jimmy Page, guitarist for Led Zeppelin, was accused by Randy California of Spirit (and his estate) of ripping off the guitar arpeggio from Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." This led to a contentious, years-long court battle that concluded at the Supreme Court in 2020, with the court ultimately rejecting the plagiarism claim. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."

xref.title: One-Night-Only Reunion (2007)
xref.body: Led Zeppelin reunited for a single, historic concert at the O2 in London on December 10, 2007. This event was prompted by the death of Ahmet Ertegun, the founder of Atlantic Records, who had signed the band in the late 1960s and was crucial to their rise. The lineup included Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones, with John's son, Jason Bonham, filling in on drums for his late father. It was the first significant appearance for Led Zeppelin in 27 years, attracting an overwhelming 20 million ticket applications. The band performed a 16-song set that night, but despite the massive success and acclaim, they have not played together again since. "On December 10th, 2007, Led Zeppelin reunited for a one night only concert at the O2 in London."

xref.title: Band Formation and Influence
xref.body: Killing Joke is described as a heavy post-punk group originating from England, which began releasing records in 1980. The band has been a significant influence on a diverse range of artists, including Tool, Nine Inch Nails, Metallica, Nirvana, the Foo Fighters, Jane's Addiction, Marilyn Manson, and Soundgarden. Additionally, Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin is noted as a massive admirer of their work. "Killing joke has been a big influence on tool, 9-inch nails, Metallica, both Nirvana and the Food Fighters, Jane's Addiction, Marilyn Manson and Soundgarden."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Claimant in "Stairway to Heaven" Lawsuit
xref.body: Randy California, the lead guitarist for Spirit, and later his estate after his death, claimed for years that Jimmy Page plagiarized Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for the iconic guitar arpeggio in Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." He sought a share of the estimated $500 million net worth of "Stairway to Heaven" through a contentious lawsuit that went all the way to the Supreme Court in 2020 before being ultimately dismissed. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."

xref.body: Classic Rock magazine in the UK has been consistently supportive of The Trews. They nominated the band for a "best new band" award for their second album at the UK Classic Rock Awards, where band members attended alongside figures like Jimmy Page and Steven Tyler. The magazine also reviewed their records and interviewed them regularly. "they nominated us for an award on our second album, like a best new band award at the UK Classic Rock Awards."

xref.title: Early Life and Musical Influences – Childhood to Age 11
xref.body: John Frusciante was born in Queens, New York, into a very musical family. His family moved multiple times, including to Tucson, Florida (where his dad was a judge), Santa Monica, and finally Los Angeles after his parents' divorce. His stepfather greatly encouraged his musical interests. His initial passion was for punk rock band The Jirms, which used unusual punk rock tuning. By age 11, he was studying the styles of David Gilmour, Jimi Hendrix, Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Frank Zappa, eventually convincing his parents to let him drop out of high school to study music full time. "He was so into guitar that he convinced his parents that he should drop out of high school and let him study music full time."

xref.title: Encounter with Jimmy Page and Occult Beliefs (Mid-1970s)
xref.body: Bowie's paranoia regarding witches stemmed from an encounter with Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page in a Manhattan townhouse. Page was known for his deep involvement in the occult, and Bowie believed that this association had put his soul in danger. "This resulted from an encounter with Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page in a Manhattan townhouse."

xref.title: Expanded Repertoire
xref.body: The band eventually broadened its repertoire beyond just Led Zeppelin songs to include material from The Yardbirds, another band associated with Jimmy Page, and Bob Marley, which made sense given their reggae style. "But Dread Zeppelin eventually expanded their repertoire to include the Yard Birds, another Jimmy Page band, and Bob Marley, which made sense, I guess."

xref.title: Filling in for Father
xref.body: Jason Bonham is the son of Led Zeppelin drummer John Bonham. He has been a member of several bands of his own and has notably sat in for his father on drums a couple of times when Jimmy Page and Robert Plant required a timekeeper. "He's not only been in a bunch of bands of his own, but he sat in for his dad on drums a couple of times when Jimmy Page and Robert Plant needed somebody to keep time."

xref.title: Influence on Guitar Legends
xref.body: His innovative guitar playing style, particularly his use of power chords, directly influenced iconic guitarists such as Jimmy Page and Pete Townshend, who picked up the guitar in part because of his sound. "Jimmy Page, Pete Townsend, guys like that picked up the guitar in part because of Link Ray."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influences from Guitar Legends
xref.body: He was influenced by Jimi Hendrix, Jimmy Page, and profoundly by Billy Gibbons of ZZ Top, drawing inspiration from Gibbons' riffage and his technique of tapping individual notes. "Billy Gibbons said it made a huge impact on Josh, not just with his riffage, but how he had a way of tapping out individual notes in the middle of everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influential Drum Teacher – Students Became Legends
xref.body: Jim Marshall became a highly respected drum teacher, and his students included several notable drummers. Among them were Mitch Mitchell, who would later become the drummer for Jimi Hendrix, and Mickey Waller, who played in bands with Jeff Beck, Rod Stewart, and Jimmy Page. "Over the years his students included Mitch Mitchell the guy who would later go on to back up Jimmy Hendrix There was Mickey Waller who played in bands with Jeff Beck and Rob Stewart and Jimmy Page."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inventor of the Power Chord
xref.body: Link Wray is credited with popularizing the idea of playing power chords on an electric guitar, a technique that would profoundly influence rock music. He is often called the "inventor of the power cord." "He has been called the inventor of the power cord, Jimmy Page, Pete Townsend, guys like that picked up the guitar in part because of Link Ray."

xref.title: Jimmy Page Hearing "Dazed and Confused"
xref.body: While Jimmy Page was a member of The Yardbirds, he heard Jake Holmes perform his song "Dazed and Confused" in 1968, which he later reworked for Led Zeppelin, leading to a plagiarism dispute. "Jimmy Page heard that version when he was still with the Artbirds."

xref.title: Jimmy Page's Occult Involvement (Mid-1970s)
xref.body: Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page was known for his deep involvement in the occult. This fascination reportedly influenced David Bowie, who believed that his association with Page had put his soul in danger, contributing to Bowie's drug-induced paranoia about witches. "Page was deep into the occult."

xref.title: Musical Development and Hard Rock Focus
xref.body: By 1967, Nancy and Ann were performing as The Viewpoints, with Nancy also doing solo shows influenced by Joni Mitchell and Paul Simon, as well as rock figures like John Lennon, Paul McCartney, Jimi Hendrix, and Jimmy Page. As their groups evolved into Heart, Nancy increasingly focused on hard rock and discovered drop D tuning, a technique that would become vital to the grunge era 15 years later. "By the time some of the various groups she was in with Ann evolved into Hart, Nancy had become much more focused on hard rock and she discovered drop D tuning, something that would become essential to the grunge era 15 years later."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneer Guitar Hero
xref.body: Eric Clapton is identified as one of the influential figures at the beginning of the "age of the guitar hero," a period in the mid-1960s when electric guitarists began to gain significant prominence and influence. "And soon we'd be hearing about Eric Clapton, Pete Townsend, Jimmy Page, Jimmy Hendrix and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Signing with Atlantic Records
xref.body: The band ultimately signed an 80/20 split deal with Atlantic Records for the world and America, while Warner Canada retained rights for Canada. This decision was influenced by the legendary status of Atlantic, known for artists like Led Zeppelin. They even met Ahmet Ertegun, one of Atlantic's co-founders, in his office on the day of signing, where they saw Jimmy Page's bow from "The Song Remains the Same" on the wall. "And so we decided to go with Atlantic records, which was the originally in our guys that we had seen that came up."
